steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Cream sugar and margarine in a large bowl until light and fluffy. Beat in eggs, one at a time, then stir in vanilla.

Combine flour, cocoa, baking soda, and salt in a separate bowl. Add to the creamed mixture and mix until just blended. Stir in walnuts. Drop spoonfuls of dough 2 inches apart onto ungreased cookie sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until edges are set and centers are soft, 8 to 10 minutes. Let sit briefly before transferring to wire racks to cool completely.

review.reviewBody: I was looking for an easy, quick fix for my husband's chocolate craving...I found it! The fact that they do taste like brownies was a bonus. They were easy to make and they were delicious. Definately drop them by the teaspoonful or less, they spread. The only problem I experienced was they stuck to my cookie sheet something aweful. Parchment paper might work, though I didn't have any...wax paper did not work. However, lightly greasing the sheet worked beautifully. I will definately make these again.

Perfect Cookie! I used butter instead of margarine and instead of walnuts added 1 cup of white chocolate chips and 1/2 cup of milk chocolate chips. I melted a bit of the butter and mixed the cocoa powder In with it then added it back to the creamed butter and sugar to cut the powdery taste many chocolate cookies have. Made the perfect cookie that was gooey in the middle and crispy around the edges

Best cookie recipe I've ever made! I added about 1.5tsp of freshly ground espresso to enhance the chocolate flavor and it worked beautifully. Also added 1 cup of chocolate chips instead of the walnuts. A 2.5 Tbsp cookie scoop made them too large I thought, so with the second batch I used the smaller scooper and felt they were a better size. Made about 3 dozen. Husband said they were the best cookies of his life!

In love with this recipe. Instead of margarine I used butter, added 1 cup of chocolate chips and sprinkled the walnuts on top before baking. I also used an ice cream scoop (3T portion scoop)to portion out my cookies since I live a big cookie. They came out perfectly.

Made these by recipe,they turned out super thin and very soft picking them up was a job,they didn't hold form of anytime. So I thought less margarine and 1/4 cup more flour,I omitted 1/4 of margarine. This time they came out actually like a brownie not falling apart of mushy,oh I also added 3 minutes to cooking time and 1/2 cup of chocolate chips.

These cookies are excellent. I substituted salted butter and I used a high quality Dutch dark chocolate cocoa powder (Droste). I substituted ground pecans instead of chopped walnuts. Pecans hardly noticeable in texture, but the flavor is there. Will chop instead of process nuts next time. I think the walnuts would make them more “brownie-like.” Baked in convection mode at 325 degrees 10-12 mins. 

Excellent cookie, tastes like a slightly crispy, lovely chewy hybrid brownie. 

My rating: ??????????

Very easy & quick to make.. I followed several reviewers & added 1/2 cup extra of FLOUR. **2 1/2 cups** The rest I followed per recipe.. My cookies came out so moist & not thin as other's have said.. It makes approx. 4 dozen + depending on 1 teaspoon each. It took 4-5 cookie sheets that I sprayed with butter cooking spray to keep my ''production line'' moving!! Baked for 10 min. My Husband loves them & it was the first time I've made them.. Will make again!!!

Delicious and pretty! I’m not sure what all the complaints are about, because these came out perfectly for me. I did chill the dough for about 30 mins first, as I do with most cookies, and I left the walnuts out since the fam doesn’t like them. A little spray of Pam on the cookie sheet kept them from sticking. My teenagers and boyfriend devoured them. One review said theirs were flat and oddly shaped, and that they wouldn’t take them to a bbq or event. I did not find this to be the case for me at all, as mine came out round and soft. I will definitely make these again!

These were very good! I made mine with butter rather than margarine. Nice thick batter! I didn’t chill the dough, so they did spread. They were on the thin side and chewy which is how I like them! Not thick or cakey at all.

I'm giving a 4 star because I didn't follow the recipe exactly as shown. I used butter instead of margarine. 2 cups instead of 2 1/4. I did a 1/4 cup of vegetable oil instead. Because of the comments I added an additional 1/4 cup of flour. I also used reeses chips instead of walnuts. I did have to let them cool a few minutes longer than chocolate chip cookies because they fell apart doing so too soon. But all in all. Solid recipe starter. Make it your own, obviously. They tasted really good. Lots of flavor. My kids loved them.

I love this recipe and had great luck with my cookies. I used very fine flour and chilled the dough between batches. I turned them into pumpkin spice cookies and they are perfect to celebrate the first day of fall with.
So delish! Perfect! I used white chic chips instead of nuts. My family thinks this is my best cookie!
Great recipe it’s a keeper. I just added a slash of maple syrup which enhanced the chocolate flavored.
Followed the recipe. Yum! My husband and I loved the chocolate flavor. I used dark chocolate.
I made these cookies yesterday morning and my family loved them so much i have to bake them again later today
Good. Like my hershey recipe better.
made it with butter instead of margarine. incredibly soft and delicious. would make again!
Flavor was okay, and I like a soft cookie, but these cookies crumbled.

I was in charge of lots baking for my Niece's destination wedding. Found this recipe when needed a quick bake with stocked ingredients. These chocolate cookies met all my requirements, very easy to make and were definitely delicious. I'm an experienced baker, however, anyone new to baking will get great results.
